modules.title: Genealogy & Traceability Engine Specification

stage_history.note: Partial build (WP-03 Document 13): a real, net-new Genealogy & Traceability Engine (app/modules/genealogy/) -- the graph engine itself: typed node/edge creation (4 of the catalogued 17 node types and 4 of the 13 edge types exercised), self-loop/duplicate-exact-edge/ancestry-cycle prevention, controlled correction (state-flip + supersedes_edge_id, never edit/delete), and the 5 read-only query APIs (lookup, ancestors, descendants, full-trace, affected-products) via a bounded BFS traversal (MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH=50; the spec's own suggestion of a recursive CTE, section 7, was not used -- an ordinary engineering substitution, not a regulated-behaviour decision). Both owned entities are DDL-ready -- the best ratio of any module yet -- and were typed directly. Full pre-existing 104-test suite passes unmodified alongside 8 new genealogy tests (112 total). Per Document 13 SS8, genealogy writes are meant to come from domain events (MaterialConsumed, DrugBatchProduced, DeviceComponentAssembled, ...) emitted by other modules; none of those producers exist yet (Material Service is WP-04; batch_execution/device emit differently-named events), so this pass built the write path as internal service functions exercised directly by tests, standing in for the consumer that doesn't exist yet -- no real production data flows into genealogy this pass (SG-052, which also covers the complaint-query dependency on WP-09, the undefined node-type-transition matrix, the unexercised migration-provenance path, and unbenchmarked performance targets). 2 of Document 13's 8 APIs (impact-assessments, exports) have no backing entity anywhere in its own 2-entity data model and were not built (SG-051). Found and fixed two real bugs during this pass: a missing TRUNCATE grant on both new tables (migration corrected in place, both DBs re-migrated), and an idempotency/duplicate-edge check that initially treated two source-event-less duplicate edges as the same idempotent replay instead of rejecting the second as a genuine duplicate (GEN-FR-023).

modules.title: Review-by-Exception & QA Review Specification

Only 1 of 3 owned entities (qa_review_package) is DDL-ready; qa_review_item and qa_review_comment are prose-only, and because nearly every itemised review behaviour in this document is modelled as one of those two entities, this is the most load-bearing single gap found so far (SG-053) -- it blocks severity classification, changed-value/override lists as rows, reviewer comments, return-for-action, checklists and multi-reviewer assignment. A further 11 requirements depend on modules that don't exist yet -- QC/material/equipment/environment review detail, genealogy-completeness rules, packaging (Document 16), yield (Document 17) -- deferred (SG-054), which also covers RBE-FR-001's own literal trigger: Document 11's batch_execution never reaches a Production Complete state, so package creation isn't gated on it this pass. Found and fixed a real bug during this pass: the completeness engine initially treated every ordinary batch lifecycle audit event (issue/start/hold, action='Changed') as a correction/exception, which would have made every batch appear to have exceptions; fixed to filter on action='Corrected' specifically -- the vocabulary genealogy's correct_edge() also uses -- which batch_execution doesn't emit yet (no correction command exists, BAT-FR-023 gapped), so the corrections signal is honestly empty today rather than wrong. Full pre-existing 112-test suite passes unmodified alongside 10 new qa_review tests (122 total, confirmed via a clean sequential run after an earlier concurrent-test-run false failure from two pytest processes racing the same test database).

modules.title: Release / Disposition Engine Specification

stage_history.note: Partial build (WP-03 Document 15): a real, net-new Release / Disposition Engine (app/modules/release/) -- evaluate a release scope (get-or-create + eligibility from real signals: QA review currency/completeness via Document 14, batch hold state, Vault execution-snapshot integrity), signature-gated release with an immediate pre-commit re-evaluation and a real Vault release-package snapshot, signature-gated hold and reject, and post-release hold/recall (REL-FR-031) that reuses the same hold command while the original RELEASED decision row is retained untouched -- tested. Unlike every module since Document 10, all 3 owned entities got typed this pass: release_scope was already DDL-ready, and release_evaluation/release_decision -- though prose-only in the catalogue -- turned out genuinely unambiguous (Document 15 even supplies a concrete JSON shape for the one semi-structured field, blockers) and were typed directly as an ordinary engineering decision (SG-045's precedent), so there is no entity-schema gap this pass. The real constraint was upstream instead: only 2 of the 9 eligibility categories REL-FR-003 names have any real data source in this codebase (QA review, Vault integrity); QC/QMS/materials/equipment/environment/packaging/genealogy/yield all depend on modules that don't exist yet, and REL-FR-002 (DDCP), REL-FR-013/014 (rework/reprocess/destruction, no route entity), REL-FR-016 (device-serial release) and REL-FR-027 (ERP/WMS) are gapped for the same reasons -- SG-055. Only scope_type='batch' is supported. Two real bugs found and fixed mid-build: the ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS check initially blocked re-evaluation entirely once a scope was on hold, contradicting REL-FR-011's 'eligibility may continue updating' while held (fixed to keep state='hold' but still refresh the evaluation); and two of the new tests had wrong hand-computed expected_version numbers (the shared eligibility-computation code always increments version, including on create) -- caught immediately by STALE_VERSION instead of the intended INVALID_TRANSITION, fixed in the test data. Full pre-existing 122-test suite passes unmodified alongside 11 new release tests (133 total), run alone (not concurrently with any other pytest process against the same test DB, after Document 14's deadlock lesson).
